summary: A dilated causal convolutional neural network (DCCNN) with 1,649 parameters enables real-time detection of charge jumps in superconducting qubits by identifying discontinuous shifts in qubit frequency during Ramsey tomography, achieving detection efficiency of $0.843 	imes 0.022$ on charge jumps of magnitude $|\_q| 	imes [0.1, 0.5] e$ at matched false-positive rate with the offline $\\\_chi^2$ baseline. The model is quantized to $\\\_mathrm{ap\\_fixed}\\\_\\\_16,6\\\_\\\_$ fixed-point arithmetic and deployed on the Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC ZCU216 via hls4ml, achieving $6.19 \_\\\_mu\\\_s$ inference latency while consuming $81.4\\\_\\%$ of available block RAM, enabling in-the-loop adaptive control protocols at NEXUS (Fermilab underground).
motivation: Charge jumps induced by cosmic-ray and gamma-ray ionization create correlated multi-qubit errors that challenge fault-tolerant quantum computing and scramble two-level systems, while simultaneously providing sensitive signatures for fundamental physics searches using qubits as particle detectors. Existing offline $\\\_chi^2$ detection methods introduce latency incompatible with real-time qubit control and show reduced sensitivity to jumps within the first $\\\sim 20$ samples of each Ramsey scan.
method: A DCCNN with four dilated causal convolution layers (filters: 8, 8, 16, 16; dilations: 1, 1, 2, 2) was trained on 100,000 synthetic Ramsey scans generated from templates measured on five qubits ($E_J/E_C = 24$, weakly charge-sensitive) at NEXUS, using quantization-aware training and a two-channel input combining raw amplitude with first-difference $\\\_Delta x_i = x_i - x_\\_{i-1}$; the model was compiled to FPGA firmware via hls4ml and integrated into QICK via AXI4-Stream/AXI4-Lite interfaces for deployment on the control timed processor (tProc).
result: On simulated 1,600-scan datasets per qubit at $1.1$ mHz jump rate, the DCCNN matched the $\\\_chi^2$ baseline mean efficiency ($0.843 \\pm 0.022$ vs. $0.866 \\pm 0.020$) while requiring zero per-qubit parameter tuning, with sustained throughput $1.65 \\times 10^5$ inferences per second and resource overhead of $+17.92\\\_\\%$ flip-flops, $+52.83\\\_\\%$ BRAM, $+19.15\\\_\\%$ LUTs, and $+36.70\\\_\\%$ DSPs relative to baseline QICK.
